c0: This is San Francisco International, rebuilt in 3D and driven by live data.
c1: The terminals, the control tower, the AirTrain and the garages are modelled from public plans, aerial imagery and open map data.
c2: Every aircraft here is a real flight, placed from its own transponder broadcasts: position, altitude and speed.
c2b: Arrivals line up on twenty-eight left and twenty-eight right, over the bay.
c3: On the ground, aircraft follow the real taxiway network, from the runway to their gate.
c3b: Jet bridges swing out and dock at the door. Stands and bridges come from OpenStreetMap and the airport's own data.
c4: Departures roll on one left and one right, and climb out over the water.
c5: Each building is drawn from published plans and measurements, then checked against aerial imagery.
c6: Weather comes from live reports. The sun and moon move with the clock, and fog and rain change what you see.
c7: At night, runway, taxiway and approach lights are placed from F A A airport data, and every aircraft carries its own lights.
c8: S F O Live 3D. The whole airport, live, in your browser.
